meanings.note: Feminine: actrice. Derived with the Romance agent/quality suffix '-eur'/'-euse' (from Latin '-or'/'-tor'). Standard masculine noun meaning 'actor'.
lowercase as an adjective; Américain(e) with a capital for a person

examples.text: Les actrices américaines ont toutes le même lifting.
examples.trans: American actresses all have the same facelift.

meanings.note: je peux t'appeler? = can I call you?
Je m'appelle Camille. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to call'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'appelé').

examples.text: Appelle Clémentine. Dis-lui que je ne peux pas venir ce soir.
examples.trans: Call Clémentine. Tell her I can't come tonight.

meanings.note: avoir peur = to be afraid, avoir raison = to be right, avoir 40 ans = to be 40

meanings.en: helper verb of the passé composé
meanings.note: J'ai appelé = I called. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to have'.

meanings.en: il y a = there is, there are
meanings.note: Fixed expression. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to have'.
as an interjection: bon, alors... = right, so...
as an interjection: bon, alors... = right, so...

meanings.en: bonne journée = have a nice day
meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'good'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

meanings.en: cardiac, related to the heart or heart conditions
meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'cardiac'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Il a eu une crise cardiaque.
Il a eu une crise cardiaque!
Oui, pour surveiller mon rythme cardiaque.
examples.trans: Yes, to monitor my heart rate.

meanings.note: Comparison: comme un rêve. Core French preposition meaning 'like', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
Conjunction. Core French preposition meaning 'like', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: C'est comme un rêve pour moi.
examples.trans: It's like a dream for me.

meanings.note: past participle of connaître used as an adjective

examples.text: Line était une chanteuse connue. Françoise était une jeune actrice.
examples.trans: Line was a well-known singer. Françoise was a young actress.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to create'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'créé').

examples.text: Ça peut créer quelque chose d'intense.
Non, ça peut créer quelque chose d'intense.
examples.trans: No, it can create something intense.

meanings.note: D' before a vowel. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
le film de Tarantino = Tarantino's film
Also 'some': du sucre. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
Demander quelque chose à quelqu'un. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to ask'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'demandé').

examples.text: Si vous avez besoin d'aide, demandez.
examples.trans: If you need help, just ask.

meanings.note: The x sounds like z before a vowel. Spoken French num expression meaning 'two', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: Deux places pour mardi? Mardi, tu as le film de Kechiche.
examples.trans: Two tickets for Tuesday? On Tuesday you've got the Kechiche film.

meanings.note: en retard = late, en vacances = on holiday

examples.text: Oh non! Je suis en retard.

meanings.note: The t is never pronounced. French conjunction meaning 'and', used to link clauses in spoken and written discourse.

examples.text: Et demain, tu déjeunes avec Audiard.
examples.trans: And tomorrow you're having lunch with Audiard.

meanings.note: for (duration): ça fait des mois que j'attends = I've been waiting for months
Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to do, to make'.

meanings.en: faire la surprise à = to surprise
meanings.note: Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to do, to make'.

meanings.en: ça fait trois semaines que = it's been three weeks since
meanings.note: With time. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to do, to make'.

examples.text: Ça fait une heure que j'attends.
examples.trans: I've been waiting for an hour.

meanings.en: to be needed, to be necessary
meanings.note: only with impersonal il: il faut + noun or infinitive

examples.text: Oui, mais il faut des autorisations. Ah, la paperasse française!
examples.trans: Yes, but you need permits. Ah, French paperwork!

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le film', plural 'les films') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'film'.

examples.text: C'est le prochain film de Tarantino.
Tu as le film de Kechiche.
Vous tournez un film aux États-Unis?
examples.trans: Are you making a film in the United States?

meanings.note: Masculine action/result noun formed with the Romance suffix '-ment' (from Latin '-mentum'). Standard masculine noun meaning 'funding, financing'.

examples.text: Le rapport du ministère sur le financement du cinéma. Pour Andréa.
examples.trans: The ministry report on cinema funding. For Andréa.

meanings.note: C'est fini = it's over. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'finished'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Tu es pourrie! Mais c'est fini.

meanings.note: for masculine nouns, and in impersonal phrases: il y a
Also in fixed phrases: il y a. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'he'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
Never changes for plural. Spoken French phrase expression meaning 'there is', common in natural conversation.
il y a trois semaines = three weeks ago

examples.text: Il y a une autre Clémentine?
Non, c'est la place de Samuel. Il est mort il y a six jours.
examples.trans: No, it's Samuel's place. He died six days ago.

meanings.note: definite article; l' before a vowel

examples.text: C'est le prochain film de Tarantino.

meanings.note: Mais oui! = of course!. French conjunction meaning 'but', used to link clauses in spoken and written discourse.
Stressed form: pour moi, avec moi. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'me'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: C'est comme un rêve pour moi.
examples.trans: It's like a dream for me.

meanings.note: ne... pas = not; ne... rien = nothing; ne... que = only; n' before a vowel

examples.text: Tarantino ne prendra pas Cécile. Problème d'âge.
examples.trans: Tarantino won't take Cécile. A problem with her age.

meanings.note: High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'we'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'we'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
A part, a permit, a result. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to get, obtain'.

examples.text: Et celle qui ne l'obtient pas va nous détester.
examples.trans: And the one who doesn't get it will hate us.

meanings.note: Faire une offre = to make an offer. Feminine noun ('la offre', plural 'les offres') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'offer'.

examples.text: C'est une offre? Je suis touché.
examples.trans: Is that an offer? I'm touched.

meanings.note: Idiomatic French interj expression meaning 'okay', frequent in natural conversational dialogue.

examples.text: OK, je vous envoie sa carte.
examples.trans: OK, I will send you her card.

examples.text: OK, comme ça tu évites de nous demander.

meanings.note: everyday speech, with a he/she verb form
General. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'we'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: On est au Westin. Tout le monde est là.
examples.trans: We're at the Westin. Everyone is here.

meanings.note: second half of ne... pas; in speech ne is often dropped

examples.text: Tarantino ne prendra pas Cécile. Problème d'âge.
examples.trans: Tarantino won't take Cécile. A problem with her age.

meanings.note: before an infinitive: pour faire plaisir
+ infinitive: pour voir. Core French preposition meaning 'for', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Je suis là pour voir Mathias.
C'est comme un rêve pour moi.
examples.trans: It's like a dream for me.

meanings.note: Masculine, although it ends in -e. Masculine noun ('le problème', plural 'les problèmes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'problem'.

examples.text: Tarantino ne prendra pas Cécile. Problème d'âge.
examples.trans: Tarantino won't take Cécile. A problem with her age.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le procédé', plural 'les procédés') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'process'.

examples.text: Ce procédé technique donne une très belle image.
examples.trans: This technical process gives a very beautiful image.

examples.text: Agir dans son dos est un procédé malhonnête.
examples.trans: Acting behind his back is an unfair tactic.

meanings.note: Cinema and television. Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'film production, producing'.

examples.text: Trois ans en production, puis deux chez VMA.
examples.trans: Three years in production, then two at VMA.

examples.text: Mais c'est toute une production! Et j'ai besoin de talons de quinze centimètres.
examples.trans: But it is a whole production! And I need fifteen-centimeter heels.

meanings.note: Un bon produit pour les cheveux. Masculine noun ('le produit', plural 'les produits') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'product'.
Produit fini. Masculine noun ('le produit', plural 'les produits') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'product'.

examples.text: Va chercher un produit pour laver le papier!
examples.trans: Go look for a product to clean the paper!

meanings.note: c'est moi qui... = I'm the one who...
Qui parle?. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'who'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.trans: I'm the one who trained you!

examples.text: Tu ne pars pas. C'est moi qui te vire!
examples.trans: You're not leaving. I'm the one firing you!

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'even'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Comme ça, on sera quittes enfin.
examples.trans: That way, we will be even finally.

examples.text: Oui, vous êtes quittes tous les deux!
examples.trans: Yes, you are both even now!

meanings.en: to leave someone, to break up with
meanings.note: Elle m'a quitté = she left me. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to leave'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'quitté').
Always with an object. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to leave'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'quitté').

examples.text: Elle est partie! Elle m'a quitté.

meanings.note: ça s'appelle = it's called; je m'appelle = my name is

examples.text: Voilà le flyer. Ça s'appelle Absence.
examples.trans: Here's the flyer. It's called Absence.

meanings.note: argent de la société = company's money
Feminine noun ('la société', plural 'les sociétés') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'company'.

examples.text: Certains ont même acheté des chaussettes avec l'argent de la société!
examples.trans: Some people even bought socks with the company's money!

examples.text: De quelle société provient ce courrier?
examples.trans: Which company does this mail come from?

meanings.note: Bonne soirée = have a nice evening. Feminine noun ('la soirée', plural 'les soirées') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'evening'.
Une soirée = an evening party. Feminine noun ('la soirée', plural 'les soirées') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'evening'.
takes a singular verb: tout le monde est là

examples.text: On est au Westin. Tout le monde est là.
examples.trans: We're at the Westin. Everyone is here.

meanings.note: travailler à Paris, travailler le dimanche

examples.text: Cannes? Tu as travaillé au festival?
examples.trans: Cannes? Did you work at the festival?

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'very'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Très bien. Et vous? Un thé?

meanings.note: one person you know well: friends, family, close colleagues

examples.text: Deux places pour mardi? Mardi, tu as le film de Kechiche.
examples.trans: Two tickets for Tuesday? On Tuesday you've got the Kechiche film.

meanings.note: ne fais pas cette tête = don't look like that; faire la tête = to sulk

meanings.en: c'est dans ma tête = it's all in my head
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la tête', plural 'les têtes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'head'.

examples.trans: Maybe it's all in my head.

meanings.note: indefinite article; des in the plural
Number; l'un = one of them. Spoken French det expression meaning 'a', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: L'un à midi, l'autre à deux heures.
examples.trans: One at noon, the other at two.

meanings.note: One person, formal. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'you'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
Several people. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'you'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
je vous rappelle = I'll call you back
Place: à Paris, à mon cours. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
Time: à midi. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

meanings.en: au = à + le, aux = à + les
meanings.note: Contractions. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
Informal for cela. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'that'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
With time. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'that'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
Masculine noun ('le échange', plural 'les échanges') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'exchange'.

examples.text: Que veux-tu en échange de ton aide?
examples.trans: What do you want in exchange for your help?

examples.text: Ça s'appelle un échange de bons procédés.

meanings.note: A person or a thing. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to avoid'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'évité').

examples.trans: I avoid coffee in the evening.

examples.text: Mais j'ai l'impression que Gabriel m'évite.
examples.trans: But I have the feeling Gabriel is avoiding me.

meanings.note: The most common verb. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to be'.
Ce + est. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to be'.
